extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, media historians, students of press ethics and anyone interested in the origins of Reuters/Thomson Reuters editorial principles
extracted.subtask_description: Describe and document the Reuters/Thomson Reuters Trust Principles and related standards for preserving editorial independence, integrity, impartiality, recruitment/training and organizational safeguards for a news agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: That Thomson Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group or faction
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall at no time pass into the hands of any one interest, group or faction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principle used to prevent concentration of control that could compromise editorial independence; historically implemented by structuring ownership as a trust (owned/financed by Press Association and NPA) to avoid dominance by a single proprietor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve integrity, independence and freedom from bias
rubrics_metrics.description: That the integrity, independence and freedom from bias of Thomson Reuters shall at all times be fully preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core ethical standard: editorial decisions and news judgement must be free of bias and influence. The article frames this as an 'unchallengeable' corporate aspiration devised by William Haley to guide future conduct and governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supply unbiased and reliable news services to a wide range of subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall supply unbiased and reliable news services to newspapers, news agencies, broadcasters and other media subscribers and to businesses, governments, institutions, individuals and others with whom Thomson Reuters has or may have contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasises reliability and impartiality across diverse clients (media and non-media). The wording implies maintaining consistent standards even when serving paying customers or contractual partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay due regard to many interests beyond the media
rubrics_metrics.description: That Thomson Reuters shall pay due regard to the many interests which it serves in addition to those of the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition that the agency serves multiple stakeholders; editorial policy should take into account various legitimate interests without compromising impartiality or media-centred responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue to expand, develop and adapt services to maintain leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: That no effort shall be spared to expand, develop and adapt the news and other services and products so as to maintain its leading position in the international news and information business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational principle: invest in coverage, products and adaptation so that standards and competitiveness are sustained; historically motivated by competition from other international agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and training standards to raise reporting quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Raise reporting standards by recruiting journalists with proven experience and introducing structured in-house training rather than relying primarily on social background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article contrasts Reuters' prior social-background-based hiring with rivals (e.g., AP) who recruited experienced reporters and applied formal training. Guidance implies merit-based hiring and formal training programs as measures of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid government interference and preserve editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not allow government payments or contracts to translate into editorial interference; retain 'absolute freedom and discretion' despite accepting state help in emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically ministers provided funds and sought that 'Reuters would bear in mind any suggestions made...on behalf of H.M. Government' — the guidance is to resist turning such suggestions into operational editorial control. Governance and culture must guard against strings attached to funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against reciprocal arrangements that risk propaganda influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid or scrutinise reciprocal news-exchange agreements with state-funded foreign agencies that could expose the agency to propaganda or partisan influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article notes Reuters exchanged stories with fascist state agencies in the 1930s, raising the risk of being a propaganda target. Guidance: assess such deals for impartiality risks and avoid arrangements that compromise independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use organisational/ownership structures (a trust) to protect independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt corporate structures (e.g., an ownership trust financed by industry bodies) designed to protect the agency's independence and prevent takeover by single interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The historical compromise created a reconstituted Reuters owned and financed as a trust by the Press Association and the Newspaper Proprietors Association; the trust structure is presented as a safeguard for editorial freedom when commercial/ political pressures exist.
